memory_update.text: For enterprise AI software/data/automation, the first-pass direct large-cap universe should include MSFT, NOW, CRM, PLTR, and SNOW as core candidates for deeper evidence checks.

The node’s strongest public-market evidence should be tracked through AI ARR/ACV, paid seat adoption, usage-based AI consumption, workflow automation outcomes, RPO/cRPO, net retention, large-customer expansion, and margin impact rather than generic AI product announcements.
Security and observability leaders were not included due to the five-candidate cap; follow-up candidates include CRWD, DDOG, ZS, PANW, MDB, ESTC, TEAM, ADBE, INTU, and PATH.

CrowdStrike deserves a near-term follow-up pass because its Q1 fiscal 2027 release reported record Q1 net new ARR and launched Charlotte AI AgentWorks with AWS, NVIDIA, and OpenAI, but it was excluded here to keep the list focused on broad enterprise software/data platforms.
NOW should remain a top enterprise-AI software candidate because it combines workflow orchestration, enterprise context, governance, and early AI ACV evidence.
SNOW maps tightly to the data-readiness and governed-context chokepoint; next pass should distinguish core consumption uplift from separately monetized AI products.
PANW is a strong security-side exposure as AI-agent deployment increases demand for identity, runtime security, DLP, and governance controls.
DDOG is a second-order AI software infrastructure supplier through LLM observability, GPU monitoring, AI-agent incident response, and compliance/cost-control telemetry.

Potential follow-up candidates not included due to 5-name limit: Varonis for data security and AI TRiSM, Zscaler for zero-trust AI data protection, CrowdStrike for AI-agent and identity security, MongoDB/Elastic for enterprise data and retrieval infrastructure, and Atlassian for developer/work-management AI workflows.
Add OKTA as an enterprise AI agent identity/security chokepoint candidate; key thesis is non-human identity governance, permissions, and auditability for agentic workflows.
Add BOX as an unstructured data readiness and content-governance candidate; thesis depends on AI attach rates and whether Intelligent Content Management accelerates revenue growth.
Add VEEV as a vertical enterprise AI software candidate; life-sciences domain context, compliance, and workflow lock-in may create stronger AI monetization than generic copilots.
Add PD as a weaker but relevant AI operations candidate; needs proof that AI-first operations can improve ARR growth and customer retention.
Add DT as an AI observability and runtime intelligence candidate; monitor whether AI-native applications create incremental usage, module adoption, and net retention.

Future Layer 1B passes should separately test data-governance/catalog vendors, low-code workflow vendors, RPA vendors, customer-support automation platforms, SI/consulting implementers, and vertical software outside life sciences.
